note: Membership as listed on each organisation's own website on the verified date. Re-check before publishing a change: membership moves.

blocs.name: African Union
blocs.founded: Launched in July 2002 in Durban, South Africa, as successor to the Organisation of African Unity, founded in May 1963 in Addis Ababa.
blocs.membersNote: The AU's own list has 55 members: these 54 countries and the Sahrawi Republic (Western Sahara), which is not one of the 54 countries this site holds figures for.

blocs.name: Economic Community of West African States
blocs.founded: Founded by the Treaty of Lagos in 1975; the treaty was revised in 1993.
blocs.membersNote: ECOWAS's member-states page lists these 12. Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger are not on it, and the page does not say why; its introduction still speaks of fifteen countries. Mauritania withdrew in December 2000.

blocs.name: East African Community
blocs.founded: The Treaty was signed on 30 November 1999 and entered into force on 7 July 2000. Somalia became a full member on 4 March 2024.

blocs.name: Southern African Development Community
blocs.founded: Began as the Southern African Development Co-ordination Conference in Lusaka on 1 April 1980. The SADC Treaty, signed in Windhoek on 17 August 1992, turned it into SADC.

blocs.name: Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa
blocs.founded: Began as the Preferential Trade Area for Eastern and Southern Africa in 1981 and became COMESA in 1994.

blocs.name: Economic Community of Central African States
blocs.founded: Founded by a treaty signed in Libreville on 18 October 1983. The treaty was revised in December 2019.

blocs.name: Intergovernmental Authority on Development
blocs.founded: Began as the Intergovernmental Authority on Drought and Development in 1986 and was relaunched as IGAD at a summit in Djibouti in November 1996.
blocs.membersNote: Eight member states. On 9 February 2026 IGAD welcomed Sudan resuming full participation after a period away.

blocs.name: Arab Maghreb Union
blocs.membersNote: Five member states. This list comes from the UN Economic Commission for Africa's profile, not from the Union's own site, which was not read.
